correctness.rationale: The shell-depth process is a nearest-neighbor walk with downward p and upward q. Its first hitting transform f=z(p+qf²) is analytic at 0; geometric mixture from the top shell gives G=z[qf+p/(2−f)]. A positive and negative square-root branchpoint at |z|=(2sqrt(pq))^(−1) yields parity-resolved n^(−3/2) tails for p<4/5; at p=4/5 f reaches 2 at the branchpoint, producing n^(−1/2); for p>4/5 a simple pole produces the displayed exponential. Return probability and mean follow from G(1),G′(1). Independent exact-rational calculation matched 88 ballot-mixture vs algebraic GF coefficients for four p values through n=22. The argument correctly restricts iid renewal to excursion lengths and does not claim iid returned coordinates.
